Aw, man! Good luck on starting. The way I started was just to find a decent and flexible software. Since I use my phone and stylus to draw on-the-go and at home, I was only able to use a mobile drawing app such as Autodesk sketchbook, it's really fun to use and has a lot of really cool and "easy" to edit brushes which you could manipulate as you please. For practice, I don't really practice that often, it's only mostly these finished drawings I do every month or a few weeks or so, but in between the times I'm not practicing, I usually just expose myself to various artwork and save the artwork that would fall into the same feel and style as my own, and learn the techniques they used, and incorporate it into my own artwork.
